items.context: @cryptojack (489.655 seguidores), en inglés: los mineros de BTC están operando a pérdida y la capitulación minera ha marcado cada gran piso de ciclo (con gráfico). Post de ~1,3 h con 41 likes, 11 respuestas y 7.411 vistas. Ángulo: economía minera y el subsidio que baja de 3,125 a 1,5625 BTC por bloque (~450 a ~225 BTC al día) en el próximo halving.
items.suggested_text:
Mining at a loss creates a very specific kind of seller. Miners pay for electricity and hardware in fiat, so when revenue drops below cost, the least efficient ones sell their reserves and eventually unplug machines. That selling isn't a view on price, it's survival, and once the weakest operators exit, difficulty adjusts down and the pressure on the rest eases.

The backdrop makes this tighter every cycle. The subsidy today is 3.125 BTC per block, roughly 450 BTC a day; at the next halving it drops to 1.5625, about 225 a day. Each cut pushes the marginal miner closer to the edge unless price or fees make up the difference.

Capitulation has lined up with bottoms before, but it's a process rather than a single day. What tends to matter more is who is still mining when it's over.
